title: SAEs-BrainMap: Unveiling the Emergence of Specialized Concepts in Deep Models via Brain Alignment
claim: Aligning sparse-autoencoder features of each model layer with brain responses reveals where concepts emerge and which layers match each cortical region.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow, dashed boxes group SAE and analysis modules
description: A wide left-to-right pipeline diagram. On the left, a stack of food photos (visual stimuli) feeds a blue 'Visual Model' made of layer columns. An arrow carries each layer's middle activation into a dashed 'Sparse Auto Encoder' box. That box has yellow trapezoids for the encoder and decoder, a blue 'Add & Relu' bar, and a sparse latent vector in the middle. Below, a brain icon with a purple circle and an fMRI scanner lead to flattened cortical maps with red ROI activations. A cosine-similarity dot node joins the SAE latent to the fMRI map. On the right, a dashed 'Model Analysis' box shows activation-similarity brain maps, Grad-CAM-style face and dog heatmaps, and a red/blue cortical 'Layer Alignment' map with a 0–11 color bar. The eye goes first to the blue and yellow SAE block.
caption: Structure of SAEs-BrainMap. We first train layer-wise SAEs to capture the monosemantic features existing in each layer, then we utilize the brain activation as a objective probe, to investigate the emergence of generic concepts in the model’s latent space. In the end, we mapping the model layers onto the brain cortex to find out the most functional correlated layer for each region.
abstract: Understanding the internal mechanisms of deep neural networks remains a significant challenge, particularly in elucidating how generic visual concepts emerge within latent spaces. In this work, we propose SAEs-BrainMap, a novel framework that utilizes human brain activation patterns from the ventral visual pathway as objective probes to guide the identification of features decomposed by Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs). Our quantitative and qualitative empirical results demonstrate a robust representational alignment between sparse model features and biological Regions of Interests (ROIs), confirming the feasibility of utilizing brain signals to characterize model functionality. By leveraging this alignment, we trace the hierarchical trajectory of generic concepts cross layers and utilize the brain's hierarchical structure to visualize the model's global processing flow, providing novel insights into model interpretability. Our code is available at this repository .
